3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: My royal yacht, the Rizania, smoothly cleaved through the waters of the Zpana river delta.

4.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
4.text: "What a great idea this boat tour was. It would have been a pity to spend our entire visit trapped in a stuffy old palace."

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: I stood on the deck next to Ewald Alphonso, President of Sordland.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: The ship's horn let out a blast as we passed beneath the bridge.

9.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
9.text: "See, this is what I like about your country. You're not afraid of the future."

10.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
10.text: "Terrific, the way you've preserved these historic buildings. But sometimes the past can be a trap."

11.speaker: Player_Romus
11.text: "Trust me, I know. I've got hundreds of years of history weighing on me every day."

12.speaker: Player_Romus
12.text: "If my grandmother hadn't made those trade deals between Rizia and Sordland, our countries would still be strangers."

13.speaker: Player_Romus
13.text: "I'm happy your country finally has a president who understands that."

14.speaker: Player_Romus
14.text: "I'm not one to look backwards. Neither are you, I hear."

15.speaker: Player_Romus
15.text: "Don't let the razzle-dazzle fool you. Rizia is as stuck in the past as it ever was."

17.speaker: Narrator
17.text: Pabel smoothly appeared from behind us with three glasses. Gus handed him the bottle.

22.speaker: Narrator
22.text: The two Sordish men smiled politely.

27.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
27.text: "Ah, yes. The free trade of Rizian wine for Sordish whiskey. As good a way as any to get our relations flowing again, if you'll pardon the pun."

28.speaker: Player_Romus
28.text: "That can't be the only reason you've traveled all this way."

29.speaker: Player_Romus
29.text: "Sordish whiskey? I'd have to taste it first."

30.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
30.text: "I was saving this until after dinner, but here you go."

31.speaker: Narrator
31.text: He opened his attache and pulled out a bottle of Erlory Maroon 30-Year-Old.

32.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
32.text: "I'll do the toast this time. How do you people say it? A proso!"

33.speaker: Narrator
33.text: We drank. The flavor rushed over my tongue -- wood smoke and forest moss tapering off to a sweet, silky smooth finish.

34.speaker: Player_Romus
34.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Prologue_Monqiz_PartyPrince"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Trait_SoberKing"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.PersonalValues_FellOffWagon"] == false) == false)

35.speaker: Player_Romus
35.text: "Disgusting. Why would anyone want a drink that tastes like trees?"
35.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Prologue_Monqiz_PartyPrince"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Trait_SoberKing"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.PersonalValues_FellOffWagon"] == false) == false)

36.speaker: Player_Romus
36.text: "It's great, but I'd better not have any more."
36.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Prologue_Monqiz_PartyPrince"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Trait_SoberKing"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.PersonalValues_FellOffWagon"] == false) == false)

37.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
37.text: "And they say royals have sophisticated palates. Your countrymen will go crazy for this."

38.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
38.text: "Like tasting the very soul of Erlory itself."

39.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
39.text: "That's liquid gold you're leaving in your glass."

40.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
40.text: "So, is it a trade, Your Majesty?"

41.speaker: Player_Romus
41.text: "Definitely. Expect to see all our bars serving Sordish whiskey by next year." [Trade Deal]

42.speaker: Player_Romus
42.text: "No. Our wine is so superior to your whiskey that it wouldn't be fair to us."

43.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
43.text: "Excellent, Your Majesty. Another reason for me to return to this gem of a country."

45.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
45.text: "You and I are meeting, aren't we? That's already progress."

46.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
46.text: "I owe a lot to Colonel Soll. But it's high time Sordland moved on."

47.speaker: Player_Romus
47.text: "My grandmother was definitely thinking ahead when she made those trade deals with Sordland years ago."

48.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
48.text: "Lyza the Great. It's not easy, living in the shadows of our predecessors."

49.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
49.text: "But if my forward-thinking development minister hadn't reconnected us, we'd still be estranged."

50.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
50.text: "Light as a feather compared to the legacy of one Colonel Soll."

51.speaker: Narrator
51.text: Gus Manger emerged from the ship's cabin, clutching a bottle and grinning triumphantly.

53.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
53.text: "I tried Cantuavo exactly once, from a Rizian chef in Holsord who smuggled it over in his steamer trunk. Haven't stopped thinking about it ever since."

55.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
55.text: "Our mutual friend Russello mentioned your yacht had an excellent wine cellar, and, well, I couldn't help myself."

56.speaker: Player_Romus
56.text: "Mr. Montoro is not my friend. And I'd appreciate it if you didn't go rooting around in my ship's quarters."

57.speaker: Player_Romus
57.text: "If you're that impressed by a Cantuavo, I hate to think of the swill they must be serving in Sordland."

58.speaker: Player_Romus
58.text: "A man of exquisite taste. I like you already."

60.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
60.text: "You hear that, Ewald! Swill! Giralt of Ribery must be spinning in his grave. Butler!"

61.speaker: Player_Romus
61.text: "Rusty has certainly sampled enough wine to know what he's talking about."

62.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
62.text: "Forgive me, Your Majesty. But we can't let this beautiful bottle go to waste now that it's been exposed to sunlight, can we? Butler!"

63.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
63.text: "I wouldn't mind gaining some firsthand knowledge myself. Butler!"

64.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
64.text: "A toast to exquisite taste, then. Butler!"

65.speaker: Pabel Adria
65.text: "Excellent choice, Mr. Manger. Please allow me."

66.speaker: Narrator
66.text: He turned his back as he filled our glasses, secretly pouring a nonalcoholic wine substitute into mine. We were used to this routine by now.

70.speaker: Narrator
70.text: He filled the glasses and handed one to each of us.

71.speaker: Pabel Adria
71.text: "This should taste of cherry and black pepper, with a faint hint of leather."

74.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
74.text: "We don't usually toast with that phrase. But nice pronunciation."

77.speaker: Narrator
77.text: We drank. Gus sighed with pure pleasure. Alphonso's expression bordered on disbelief.

78.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
78.text: "All apologies to Giralt of Ribery, but this is in fact the best wine I've ever tasted."

79.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
79.text: "I told you! I know certain Sordish movers and shakers who'd kill to have access to a beverage of this caliber."

80.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
80.text: "Which brings me to that deal I suggested..."

81.speaker: Player_Romus
81.text: "Rizians do not drink whiskey, Mr. President."

82.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
82.text: "Our turn to be the connoisseurs, Your Majesty. Butler! Three tumblers, no ice."

87.speaker: Player_Romus
87.text: "Just a small sip for me. To make sure my people aren't getting an inferior product."

88.speaker: Player_Romus
88.text: "Actually, I'll take your word for it. The wine's already gone to my head."

89.speaker: Player_Romus
89.text: "If I didn't know any better, I'd say you two were trying to get me drunk."

91.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
91.text: "One does not get merely 'drunk' on Erlory Maroon 30-Year-Old. One floats."

92.speaker: Player_Romus
92.text: "I hope this is as good as you say."

95.speaker: Narrator
95.text: Alphonso opened his attache and pulled out a bottle of Erlory Maroon 30-Year-Old.

97.speaker: Narrator
97.text: The yacht lingered at the mouth of the Zpana delta as the sun lowered in the sky, turning the water from turquoise to gold.

98.speaker: Narrator
98.text: A series of looks passed between Gus and Alphonso. They turned back to me.

100.speaker: Player_Romus
100.text: "Yes, sure. Now can we get to the real reason why you're here?" [Trade Deal]

101.speaker: Player_Romus
101.text: "No, sorry. I'd rather not bring more hard liquor into this country."

102.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
102.text: "A shame, Your Majesty. But I do have one more proposal for you."

104.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
104.text: "Excellent, Your Majesty. And yes, there is one more proposal we wanted to discuss."

105.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
105.text: "As much as Sordland's most valued citizens would appreciate your wine, we believe there's something else they'd find even more stunning."

106.speaker: Narrator
106.text: He gestured at his surroundings, then down at the short-sleeved shirt he was wearing.

107.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
107.text: "Have you thought about Rizia's untapped tourism potential, Your Majesty?"

108.speaker: Player_Romus
108.text: "I'm afraid our conflicts with our neighbors would scare off visitors."

109.speaker: Player_Romus
109.text: "Yes, many times. Our beaches put Lespia's to shame, after all."

110.speaker: Player_Romus
110.text: "We only want the right kind of tourists, Mr. Manger. No riff-raff."

112.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
112.text: "I took the liberty of hiring a designer to draw this up."

116.speaker: Narrator
116.text: He reached inside his jacket pocket and pulled out a sheet of paper with a sketch on it.

117.speaker: Narrator
117.text: I recognized the beach it depicted. It was a picturesque stretch of sand in Monqiz, not far from the palace where I'd grown up.

118.speaker: Narrator
118.text: Right on the coastline, the designer had placed a sprawling complex with a swimming pool and tennis courts. On it was a sign: "Koronti Resort Valenqiris."

119.speaker: Player_Romus
119.text: "House Toras would never stand for this."

120.speaker: Player_Romus
120.text: "No. I'm not bringing Sordish new money to Rizia."

121.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
121.text: "New money, old money -- it's all money. And the investors behind this proposal are itching to spend theirs here."

123.speaker: Player_Romus
123.text: "Would that be the senior or the junior Koronti?"

124.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
124.text: "It's only a rough sketch, Your Majesty. But yes, a private pier would go without saying."

125.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
125.text: "You are the head of House Toras, are you not?"

126.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
126.text: "You've done your research, I see. This is Marcel's initiative. Along with certain other members of the Lotherberg Group."

127.speaker: Narrator
127.text: Alphonso swirled the last drops of whiskey around in his glass.

128.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
128.text: "I'm aware of how your nobles see Sordish oligarchs. I'm also aware that their world-renowned riches have diminished with each successive generation."

129.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
129.text: "Change is not merely inevitable, Your Majesty -- it's the only way to preserve the lifestyle to which you're all so accustomed. Your grandmother understood that."

130.speaker: Player_Romus
130.text: "Lyza wouldn't have wanted a bunch of fat, sunburned vulgarians blocking her ocean views. No offense."

131.speaker: Player_Romus
131.text: "We don't need Sordland's help to stay wealthy."

132.speaker: Player_Romus
132.text: "I am the king. The nobles would have no choice but to acquiesce."

133.speaker: Player_Romus
133.text: "Well said, Mr. President. My relatives could use a good shock to the system."

135.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
135.text: "So that's a yes on the proposal?"

136.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
136.text: "Our partners are considering significant investment along the Valenqiris coast. If all went well, the Koronti resort would only be the first step."

137.speaker: Narrator
137.text: Gus drew his breath in through his teeth.

138.speaker: Player_Romus
138.text: "It is indeed. I hope I'm invited to the grand opening." [Resort Deal]

139.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
139.text: "You too, eh? We'll assume that's a no on the proposal, then."

140.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
140.text: "We know you've got Queen Beatrice providing her protection. We just wanted to offer you some extra insurance."

141.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
141.text: "But we'll assume that's a no on the proposal, then?"

142.speaker: Player_Romus
142.text: "Well... I don't like it, but I'd be a fool to turn down your oligarchs' investment. The answer is yes." [Resort Deal]

143.speaker: Player_Romus
143.text: "You're already getting our wine. That's enough wheeling and dealing for one day."

147.speaker: Player_Romus
147.text: "No, indeed. Come back when you have better ideas."

149.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
149.text: "The King will get a free stay in the largest suite. Anytime he likes."

150.speaker: Player_Romus
150.text: "Yes. As long as the final design is less gaudy." [Resort Deal]

151.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
151.text: "I'll pass that on to our partners."

152.speaker: Player_Romus
152.text: "No. I do want to open Rizia up to the world, but I'd rather explore other avenues."

154.speaker: Player_Romus
154.text: "Your assumption is correct. Sorry to waste your time."

157.speaker: Narrator
157.text: They glanced at each other in surprise.

158.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
158.text: "Well. I'm glad we have an understanding!"

163.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
163.text: "One trade deal is already more than our predecessors managed in 30 years."

164.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
164.text: "So the door between our countries will remain closed. For now, at least."

169.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
169.text: "In less than an hour, we've accomplished more for our countries than our predecessors managed in 30 years."

170.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
170.text: "If the wine will not come to Sordland, Sordland will come to the wine. I'm satisfied with that."

171.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
171.text: "Rusty led me to believe you were more open-minded than your father. A shame."

172.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
172.text: "There's only one opportunity that matters to me right now. Butler! Another bottle!"

173.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
173.text: "But no wine in Sordland means that we'd better get our fill of Cantuavo while we're here. Butler! Another bottle!"

174.speaker: Player_Romus
174.text: "His name is Pabel Adria. Show some respect."

175.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
175.text: "Yes, that alone calls for a celebration. Butler! Another bottle!"

176.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
176.text: "I'd say that calls for a celebration. Butler! Another bottle!"

179.speaker: Narrator
179.text: Pabel reappeared, another bottle in his hands. He filled our glasses with a look of annoyance that only I could detect.

180.speaker: Narrator
180.text: Pabel reappeared, another bottle in his hands. He shot me a grateful look as he filled our glasses.

185.speaker: Narrator
185.text: Pabel reappeared, another bottle in his hands. He filled our glasses, a neutral expression on his face.

186.speaker: Narrator
186.text: The yacht began to turn back towards Porte Drazon as the sun disappeared over the horizon.

187.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
187.text: "The Colonel was no great fan of monarchies, as you'll recall. Me? I'm more flexible."

188.speaker: Player_Romus
188.text: "For such an anti-monarchist, he behaved an awful lot like a king."

189.speaker: Player_Romus
189.text: "The only difference between your republic and our monarchy is that the Rizian people are happier."

190.speaker: Player_Romus
190.text: "Nor was my father keen on democracy. You and I have much in common."

191.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
191.text: "Are you sure that's not just because of your splendid weather?"

192.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
192.text: "Gus said he thought we'd get along. Speak of the devil."

193.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
193.text: "By the end, maybe. I wish we'd parted ways on better terms."

195.speaker: Player_Romus
195.text: "Countries with differing politics can still find common ground."

199.speaker: Player_Romus
199.text: "That's enough, Mr. Manger. I'm cutting you off."

203.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
203.text: "I'll see you in Sordland, then, beautiful."

204.speaker: Narrator
204.text: He waved a wistful goodbye to the bottle Pabel was holding in his hands. My butler gave a brisk, professional nod and disappeared back into the cabin.

205.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
205.text: "I'll see you on our next visit, then, beautiful."

206.speaker: Narrator
206.text: After hours of diplomatic formalities in Palas Rezna, the sea breeze felt amazing. Alphonso removed his jacket and looked up admiringly at the wide cable bridge that connected Porte Drazon's two halves.

207.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
207.text: "A beautiful, elegant old palace. Your Majesty."

209.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
209.text: "I know one man who's happy for a clean break, though."

211.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
211.text: "Last I saw, your treasury crone was in the cabin reading over the terms of the proposal. Shall we haul her up and hash this out?"

215.speaker: Player_Romus
215.text: "You're in Rizia. Mr. Manger. We treat women like equals here."

216.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
216.text: "Since your treasury crone isn't here to put a damper on proceedings, should we get straight to it?"

217.speaker: Player_Romus
217.text: "Don't call Ms. Werner a crone. She's one of my most capable councilors."

218.speaker: Player_Romus
218.text: "Sorry I had to bring along the wet blanket. I would've preferred a men's night out, too."

220.speaker: Player_Romus
220.text: "You're in Rizia. Mr. Manger. We treat women like equals here."

224.speaker: Narrator
224.text: Pabel poured me a small amount with an apologetic shrug.

225.speaker: Narrator
225.text: Pabel poured us each a small amount of the amber-colored liquid.

229.speaker: Narrator
229.text: It was my first taste of alcohol since my wilder days. Visions of broken villa windows and weekend-long blackouts came to me unbidden.
229.conditionsRaw: (Variable["RiziaDLC.Prologue_Monqiz_PartyPrince"] == true) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Trait_SoberKing"] == true) and ((Variable["RiziaDLC.PersonalValues_FellOffWagon"] == true) == false)

233.speaker: Narrator
233.text: The taste brought back memories of my wilder days. Visions of broken villa windows and weekend-long blackouts came to me unbidden.

234.speaker: Player_Romus
234.text: "Don't call Ms. Werner a crone. She's one of my most capable councilors."

235.speaker: Narrator
235.text: Alphonso gave Gus a look of warning.

236.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
236.text: "I apologize on behalf of my minister. I told him to leave his baser impulses at home."

237.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
237.text: "It could have been worse. Imagine if Nia Morgna were here, Gus."

238.speaker: Player_Romus
238.text: "Yes, let's work this out between us men. No wet blanket necessary."

239.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
239.text: "'You can't bring the King whiskey, Mr. President! That's bribery!'"

240.speaker: Narrator
240.text: Gus laughed and shifted his voice to a higher register.

241.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
241.text: "I assure you Sordland is making progress on the status of women. Some of my most trusted ministers belong to the fairer sex."

242.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
242.text: "I'm glad you understand. Imagine if Nia Morgna were here, Gus."

243.speaker: Narrator
243.text: Pabel ducked into the ship's cabin and re-emerged with Elena. My treasury councilor looked slightly seasick.

247.speaker: Elena Werner
247.text: "Pardon my absence, gentlemen. Despite my Valgish ancestry, I never warmed up to boat travel."

248.speaker: Elena Werner
248.text: "The draft agreement seems sound. But I had a question about the section regarding quantities."

249.speaker: Elena Werner
249.text: "You're proposing an equal amount of wine and whiskey be traded per year, when more demand currently exists for the former than the latter."

250.speaker: Player_Romus
250.text: "If demand for whiskey doesn't exist in Rizia, we'll just have to find a way to create it."

251.speaker: Player_Romus
251.text: "See, this is why I brought her along."

252.speaker: Player_Romus
252.text: "Is there another way we can rephrase this, Mr. President?"

253.speaker: Narrator
253.text: Alphonso reopened his briefcase and took out some paperwork.

255.speaker: Player_Romus
255.text: "Reopening trade channels to sell us useless whiskey. What a swindle."

256.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
256.text: "The governments of Rizia and Sordland, recognizing the importance of promoting economic growth and cooperation and desiring to enhance their mutual interests..."

257.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
257.text: "...conducted in a manner that is consistent with their respective domestic laws and regulations..."

258.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
258.text: "...the parties shall agree to cooperate in the development and implementation of sanitary measures..."

259.speaker: Player_Romus
259.text: "Sounds legitimate. No need to go on."

263.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
263.text: "...elimination of tariffs to be completed within six months from the entry into force..."

264.speaker: Player_Romus
264.text: "Seems straightforward enough. Here's what I've decided."

265.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
265.text: "...ensuring that respective customs procedures and other trade-related measures are transparent, efficient and predictable..."

269.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
269.text: "...in equal amounts of 100 tons of wine and 50 barrels of whisky per year, subject to availability..."

271.speaker: Player_Romus
271.text: "Okay. Here's what I want to do."

272.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
272.text: "Phew. I thought that would never end."

273.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
273.text: "A wise move, Your Majesty. The fine print goes on forever."

275.speaker: Player_Romus
275.text: "Equal amounts? Demand for Rizian wine in Sordland is far higher than that for Sordish whiskey in Rizia."

278.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
278.text: "We can change that section if you like. 'Quantities subject to market demand.'"

279.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
279.text: "It won't be difficult. This whiskey speaks for itself."

280.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
280.text: "Demand in Rizia will skyrocket once Erlory Maroon hits the market. Trust me."

286.speaker: Narrator
286.text: Elena raised her eyebrows but stayed silent. Gus and Alphonso exchanged a series of looks, then turned back to me.

290.speaker: Narrator
290.text: Elena flipped open her ledger and made a quick note.

294.speaker: Narrator
294.text: Elena flipped open her ledger and made a quick note.

295.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
295.text: "I know that for a long time, international tourists stayed away from the Valenqiris coast because of the delicate situation with Pales."

296.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
296.text: "Porte Drazon is gorgeous enough. But your beaches!"

301.speaker: Player_Romus
301.text: "Yes, relations with *pall-ey* have been shaky for years."

302.speaker: Narrator
302.text: He pronounced the last word as "pails."

305.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
305.text: "Oh. Sorry, I've never had the occasion to speak the name aloud."

306.speaker: Narrator
306.text: He didn't seem to notice my correction.

307.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
307.text: "My point is that it might finally be time to bring your underdeveloped shores to life."

308.speaker: Player_Romus
308.text: "Not so fast. Let me confer with Elena."

312.speaker: Narrator
312.text: The Sordish visitors waited outside as Elena and I walked into the cabin to talk.

315.speaker: Player_Romus
315.text: "This is exactly what I was worried about. Sords waltzing in here and disrespecting our nobility."

316.speaker: Player_Romus
316.text: "You served under Queen Lyza. Would she have wanted this?"

317.speaker: Elena Werner
317.text: "If I may speak freely... I don't think it's a bad idea."

318.speaker: Elena Werner
318.text: "Their attitude leaves something to be desired, yes."

319.speaker: Elena Werner
319.text: "Well... Lyza did everything in her power to transform Rizia into a modern, enlightened nation. But she was also a proud Toras."

320.speaker: Elena Werner
320.text: "I'm not sure she would have wanted to see her house's pride and joy become a stomping ground for Sords."

321.speaker: Elena Werner
321.text: "But if I may speak freely... I don't think it's a bad idea."

323.speaker: Player_Romus
323.text: "Okay. That's all I wanted to know."

324.speaker: Player_Romus
324.text: "You're not a Toras. You don't understand."

325.speaker: Elena Werner
325.text: "I do, though. You must remember that I'm from Valenqiris."

326.speaker: Elena Werner
326.text: "You must remember that I'm from Valenqiris."

327.speaker: Elena Werner
327.text: "I grew up just minutes away from those beaches, but it wasn't until I became a councilor that I had the pull to bring my family there."

328.speaker: Player_Romus
328.text: "Neither do I. But I wanted to hear your reasoning."

329.speaker: Elena Werner
329.text: "Monqiz is far enough up the coast that it'd be insulated from any fighting. We might have a problem if the Sords take Pales' side."

330.speaker: Elena Werner
330.text: "That resort wouldn't just open the Valenqiris coast up to Sordland. It'd open it up to the rest of Rizia."

331.speaker: Elena Werner
331.text: "Then again, the obscenely wealthy have never had a problem with going on holiday in politically objectionable territory."

332.speaker: Elena Werner
332.text: "Shall we get back out on deck?"

334.speaker: Player_Romus
334.text: "We shall. Thank you for sharing your opinion."

336.speaker: Narrator
336.text: We stepped back out into the waning sunlight and rejoined Alphonso and Gus Manger.

337.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
337.text: "Well, Your Majesty? Are we making history today?"

338.speaker: Player_Romus
338.text: "You have a deal. But does the resort have to be as gaudy as the one in the picture?"

339.speaker: Player_Romus
339.text: "Just remember to invite me to the grand opening of the Koronti Resort Valenqiris."

340.speaker: Player_Romus
340.text: "One deal is enough for today, gentlemen."

344.speaker: Player_Romus
344.text: "I'm afraid neither of your proposals appeal to me. Sorry to send you home with nothing."

345.speaker: Player_Romus
345.text: "No, our coastline shall stay the way it is. Untouched by foreign influence."

350.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
350.text: "Ha. I'm sure our architects can come up with something more subtle."

351.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
351.text: "You'll get a free stay in the largest suite. Anytime you like."

353.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
353.text: "That's still more than our predecessors managed in the past 30 years. And it leaves the door open for more dialogue."

357.speaker: Elena Werner
357.text: "One trade deal is still quite the feat."

362.speaker: Elena Werner
362.text: "Yes, please do get in touch should further trade opportunities arise."

366.speaker: Elena Werner
366.text: "We're still open to other trade opportunities. Please get in touch if any arise."

367.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
367.text: "Nothing to do but drown our sorrows. Butler! Another bottle!"

368.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
368.text: "I stand corrected. Mr. Adria, if you would be so kind."

369.speaker: Narrator
369.text: I tasted mine: nothing but juice. Somehow, he had still managed to perform the switch.

390.speaker: Player_Romus
390.text: "That's exactly what my relatives are worried about."

391.speaker: Player_Romus
391.text: "The resort is still private property. Commoners would barely be able to afford it."

392.speaker: Player_Romus
392.text: "Unless we get back into another conflict with 'Pails.'"

394.speaker: Elena Werner
394.text: "But if they did have the money, they'd be able to get in. There's the difference."

395.speaker: Elena Werner
395.text: "Yes, the rest of your house wouldn't love it. But you'd still have lots of coastline to call your own."

400.speaker: Narrator
400.text: I relished the bite. I could almost feel myself slipping back into my old, dangerous habits.

404.speaker: Narrator
404.text: It was my first taste of alcohol in years. I was surprised by how pleasurable it was.
404.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["RiziaDLC.Prologue_Monqiz_PartyPrince"] == true) == false) and (Variable["RiziaDLC.Trait_SoberKing"] == true  and  Variable["RiziaDLC.PersonalValues_FellOffWagon"] == false)

411.speaker: Player_Romus
411.text: "Well... I can't say no to Sordish hospitality. I'll just have a little taste."

415.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
415.text: "I say that means more for us, Ewald."

417.speaker: Narrator
417.text: Pabel poured each of the two Sords a small amount of the amber-colored liquid.

418.speaker: Ewald Alphonso (R)
418.text: "I'll do the toast this time. How do you people say it? A proso!"

419.speaker: Narrator
419.text: They drank. A smile spread across Gus' face.

420.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
420.text: "That dark, woodsy flavor, that silky-smooth finish. You're really missing out, Your Majesty."

423.speaker: Player_Romus
423.text: "Just as well. If it's as good as you say, I'd never be able to stop drinking it."

424.speaker: Gus Manger (R)
424.text: "Your countrymen will go crazy for it, I promise."
